title: To Cross, or Not to Cross Pages for Prefetching?
problem: L1D cache prefetchers operating with virtual addresses can issue prefetch requests across page boundaries, but whether page-cross prefetching is beneficial or harmful is workload- and phase-dependent, and existing prefetchers lack the intelligence to selectively enable or suppress these cross-page requests.
motivation: State-of-the-art L1D prefetchers produce inaccurate page-cross prefetches that pollute caches and waste TLB resources, yet completely disabling them also misses legitimate performance gains, motivating a dynamic, workload-aware decision mechanism.
method: MOKA is a holistic framework for designing Page-Cross Filters that attach to existing L1D prefetchers. It combines three components: (i) hashed perceptron predictors using prefetcher-independent program features (PC, stride, memory access history) to estimate page-cross benefit, (ii) system-state-adaptive predictors that account for TLB pressure and MSHR occupancy, and (iii) a dynamic phase-switching scheme that periodically recalibrates filter decisions across changing execution phases. The resulting prototype filter, DRIPPER, is instantiated for Berti, IPCP, and BOP prefetchers without modifying their core logic.
key_novelty: A systematic, predictor-agnostic framework (MOKA) for selectively gating page-cross prefetch requests using phase-adaptive hashed perceptron predictors that account for both program features and live system state.
contributions: Comprehensive characterization showing page-cross L1D prefetching is rarely beneficial and often harmful across 218 workloads
MOKA framework unifying design principles for Page-Cross Filters applicable to any L1D prefetcher
DRIPPER, a concrete filter implementation that improves geomean performance over both always-cross and never-cross strategies
Demonstration of consistent benefits across both 4KB and 2MB huge page configurations

metrics.speedup: 1.7% over always-cross Berti (single-core); 2.5% over never-cross Berti; 2.0%/3.3% geomean on 8-core mixes vs always/never-cross

limitations: Evaluation focuses on single-threaded and 8-core multiprogrammed workloads; server-scale NUMA or accelerator-coupled scenarios are not explored.
primary_theme: Selective page-cross prefetch filtering for L1D caches
